Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

temporary adjective

also temporarily, provisional, short-term, makeshift

classical

Cic. Off. 1.27: brevis est et ad tempus
Liv. 28.42.5: dux ad tempus lēctus (Lewis & Short)

ad tempus

phrase

for a time, temporary

The classical way to say it: what is ad tempus lasts for a time, for the moment. The same words also mean “at the right time, on time” (ad tempus redīre, Cic. Att. 13.45.2, Lewis & Short; see on time); the context tells which.

Other words

  • in tempus — for the time being, for the occasion

    phrase · also used · classical · Tac. Ann. 14.20: scaenā in tempus strūctā; Traupman 88–89: for the occasion, for the time being, in tempus; Traupman 394

  • temporārius, temporāria, temporārium — lasting only for a time

    adjective · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 9.9: amīcitiae, quās temporāriās populus appellat · Declension on Wiktionary

    Rare before Augustus (Nepos once); Seneca, the elder Pliny, Quintilian (Lewis & Short). It also means suited to the times, and so changeable: temporāria līberālitās (Nep. Att. 11), ingenia temporāria (Curt. 4.5.11).

  • subitārius, subitāria, subitārium — makeshift, put together in a hurry

    adjective · also used · classical · Tac. Ann. 14.20: subitāriīs gradibus; Tac. Ann. 15.39: subitāria aedificia (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of what is got up in haste for an emergency: temporary shelters, stands, troops raised at short notice (subitāriī mīlitēs, Livy). Lewis & Short.

  • prō tempore — given for “for the time being”

    avoid · classical · Sall. Jug. 49.6: pauca prō tempore mīlitēs hortātus (Lewis & Short s.v. hortor); Traupman 109, 394

    In classical prose prō tempore is “to suit the occasion, as time allowed” (see occasion); for “for the time being” say ad tempus or in tempus (above), or in praesentiā (see now).

Examples

  • perturbātiōne aliquā animī, quae plērumque brevis est et ad tempus

    in some upset of the mind, which is mostly brief and temporaryCic. Off. 1.27

  • nam anteā subitāriīs gradibus et scaenā in tempus strūctā lūdōs ēdī solitōs

    for (they said) games used to be given before on makeshift tiers, with a stage put up for the occasionTac. Ann. 14.20

  • Hae sunt amīcitiae, quās temporāriās populus appellat

    These are the friendships that people call temporarySen. Ep. 9.9

See also permanent, short, now, moment.
